title: Router guardrail: threshold-gating and automated cutover for region/tier/model variants
creator: Alex Chen
description: Design and implement a router-level guardrail that gates traffic based on automated thresholds (429 spikes, p99 latency timeouts, request error-rate) and performs an automated cutover to safe model variants or alternate regions/tiers when thresholds are breached. This ticket covers policy semantics, signal aggregation, fast-path circuit gating, and a gradual rollback/cutover orchestration to avoid oscillation and customer-visible flapping.
acceptance_criteria: Router exposes a configurable threshold-gate policy per route: (429_rate, p99_latency_ms, error_rate) with short- and long-window evaluation windows

When short-window threshold is exceeded, router enters a guarded state and can automatically shift up to two fallback actions: degrade model variant -> route to dedicated fallback tier -> failover to alternate region (configurable order)
Circuit gate prevents repeated automated cutovers for the same route for a cool-down period configurable per policy
All state transitions are logged and emitted to observability pipeline (Datadog/OTLP) with tags: route, project, customer_id, from_variant, to_variant, trigger_metric
Rollout of policy supports canary (X% of traffic), ramp, and a manual override in Console
Automated ABORT path: if fallback increases error-rate or latency further, router reverts to original variant and opens a PagerDuty incident with context
Unit/integration tests for gating logic + e2e scenario harness showing failover on synthetic 429 spike
Documentation in Console config docs and ops runbook completed and reviewed by SRE and Product
implementation_notes: Policy evaluation happens in router edge immediately after request admission; use a two-window aggregator: 10s short-window, 5m long-window
Signals: 429_count / request_count (short), p99_latency_ms (histogram snapshot), 5xx error fraction (long)
Use existing per-route KV store (consistent hash) to persist gate state; store: open_until, last_trigger, active_fallback
Circuit gate semantics: OPEN -> PROBATION -> CLOSED. OPEN when short-window breach; PROBATION after cool-down with controlled sample traffic; CLOSED when stable metrics for long-window

Fallback orchestration: prefer local model variants (quantized/low-cost) first, then tier downgrade (from dedicated->shared), then regional failover. All steps must respect customer constraints (region pinned, private deployments disabled)
Backoff and jitter on automated cutover to avoid thundering herd when many routes flip simultaneously
Expose a dry-run mode where router simulates gating decisions and emits events but does not cut traffic
Implementation to be done in two phases: Phase 1 (policy engine + local fallback variant) Phase 2 (tier and region failover plumbing + Console controls)
Integrate with rollout service to support canary percentages and TTL-based overrides
Add feature flag gate to enable/disable per-customer via org config
observability_and_metrics: add tracing span 'router.guardrail.evaluate' with tags for threshold values and decision path
dashboards: Guardrail Overview (active gates, triggers over time), Per-route timeline, and Customer Impact heatmap
alert: guardrail_open_rate > 1% of routes in OPEN for 10m -> paging to SRE
logging: structured event to /events/routing/guardrail with correlation_id and sample request payload (scrubbed)
SLO considerations: ensure guardrail activations do not by themselves cause SLO violations; add synthetic checks post-cutover
rollout_plan: Dev: unit tests + router simulation harness (merge to feature branch)
Stage: enable dry-run for 100% of traffic for 48h, compare events and model switch delta metrics
Canary: enable active gating for 5% of routes (based on low-risk prefix) for 24h, monitor error-rate and customer impact
Ramp: 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 1 week with daily checkpoints
Full: enable auto-cutover by default, keep manual override in Console for 72h
Rollback: feature flag off to revert gating; runbook steps to manually revert individual route states
Postmortem: after any unintended customer impact, require incident review and freeze additional rollouts
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: oscillation between variants causing increased latency - Mitigation: probation sampling and exponential backoff
Risk: false positives from bursty 429s - Mitigation: short-window threshold plus long-window confirmation before region failover
Risk: violating customer pinning (region/model) - Mitigation: policy honors route/customer constraints and never overrides explicit pins
Risk: increased cost from tier downgrades or cross-region egress - Mitigation: add budget guard and cost-aware scoring in policy evaluation
Risk: observability blind spots - Mitigation: require emitted events for every decision and unit tests that assert event shape
open_questions: What exact default threshold values should we ship with? (suggestions: 429_rate_short>1% in 10s, p99_latency>1200ms short)
Should per-customer policies be editable via API or Console only?
How to score fallback options when multiple compatible variants exist? (cost-first vs latency-first vs availability-first)
How do we surface cost implications to product owners when an automated cutover will increase per-token cost?
Do we need legal/finance signoff for cross-region failovers that move data outside customer region?
